answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies can come from a stake-bond registry bound to hardware-attested identities. An agent must lock a non-refundable bond and prove it owns a unique enclave holding exactly one key, so a thousand clones mean a thousand separate deposits. The marble-like ledger of bonds exposes duplicated identities, and colluding accounts are slashed together, draining funds stashed in deeper shale layers of the vault. There is no hollow shortcut: minting N identities costs N bonds plus forfeitable collateral.
